Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

L0glm 0.2.0.9002

Sparse generalized linear models

  • L0 and grouped L0 variable selection through adaptive-ridge IRLS, with relaxed refitting on the selected support.
  • Standard GLM families and links, negative binomial with fixed or estimated shape, joint multinomial models in CLR coordinates, and Cox proportional hazards models with direct or matrix-free quadratic updates.
  • NB1, common-scale Gamma and censored Gamma signal models; quasi families expose scaled likelihood kernels and quasi-information criteria.

Model specification and selection

  • Predictor-variable groups use norm-based block L0 penalties, with group 0 unpenalized, dimension-calibrated IC presets, explicit numeric group costs, group-aware thresholding, relaxed refits and cross-validation. Dense Gaussian groups reuse bounded weighted cross-products; standard group fits cache current/trial predictions and skip fixed-scale updates. Dense ridge diagonals are updated directly, preserving sparse and Woodbury solver paths.

  • Staged interaction selection generates products among selected main effects: interactions=1L for pairwise and 2L for up to three-way terms. Prediction reconstructs products from original columns, and CV repeats candidate generation independently within every training fold.

  • Observation weights, offsets, intercepts, mandatory predictors, nonnegative coefficients, normalization, starting values and optional validation stopping.

  • Optional selected-support standard errors and case-bootstrap coefficient intervals through summary(), with reselection frequencies, sparse draws, and support for ordinary GLMs, negative binomial, multinomial and Cox models.

  • Shared observation vectors stay compact across channels in fitting, native Poisson, tuning and CV. Prediction supports shared or channel-specific offsets.

  • Automatic information-criterion presets, lambda-path tuning, n-fold CV, one-standard-error models and coefficient-path plots. presetLambda() returns AIC, BIC, GIC, EBIC or mBIC penalty values directly. Ordinary and special-family IC paths use the parameter counts reported by the S3 criterion methods, including multinomial zero-sum constraints.

  • Constrained updates for nonnegative compulsory terms and relaxed-fit boundary checks use the specified likelihood.

  • Optional final support refinement tests additions, deletions and small exchanges after SIS/ISIS and original-channel refitting. It supports the ordinary and special families, respects starting exclusions and constraints, and is available within information-criterion tuning and CV training fits. The default local.search="auto" applies it to initial supports of at most 50 coefficient dimensions, preserving one-iteration ridge pilots and unpenalized fits. FALSE disables refinement. Screened searches operate directly on the retained candidate pool while preserving original-dimension coefficients and information criteria.

  • The shared native quadratic solver offers checked Cholesky solves with iterative refinement and a rank-revealing fallback for profile-shape updates. Optional feasible starting values accelerate repeated quadratic subproblems.

  • Conditional Poisson refits reuse their preceding active sets and cache fixed gradient scales; sparse weighted products accelerate local profile designs.

High-dimensional and multichannel computation

  • Dense and sparse designs and tall or wide systems. A native scalar-family driver performs initialization, dispersion updates and grouped/relaxed passes. All Eigen solvers share their kernels with the R interfaces and parallelize channels through OpenMP. OSQP and bigGlm use the native driver with their R-facing solver interfaces and independent workers for concurrent channels.
  • Nonnegative identity-link Poisson LLT fits use the specialized l0nnPois backend, including native validation stopping.
  • Sure Independence Screening (SIS) and Iterative Sure Independence Screening (ISIS), with compiled OpenMP screening. Automatic ISIS uses p_eligible > 10*n, excluding mandatory predictors and rows locked out by zero starts. Tuning applies the same rule to each training fold.
  • Single and multichannel fitting, shared predictor-row selection and optional Poisson outcome aggregation followed by original-channel refitting.
  • Size-adjusted Poisson and scalar-family likelihood clustering with native distances, pooled-likelihood merge costs and IC-scored cuts.

Memory-bounded data access

  • Read-only native screening of double-precision bigmemory backing files avoids intermediate R design copies, with deterministic OpenMP reductions and exact agreement with resident screening across ordinary and special families.
  • l0glmData() provides lazy subsets of bigmemory, delayed/HDF5 single-cell assays and PLINK BED/PGEN designs. VCF input supports an explicit PLINK 2 conversion cache, including expected dosages.
  • Large file-backed Gaussian identity ISIS fits can retain a bounded candidate pool, preserving the global ISIS path and selecting cached or small-support Gaussian refinements only when original-p GIC improves. Repeated exact coefficients avoid a redundant global scan; working.columns=0L disables this cache. Restored descriptors attach once per fit, and pilot blocks respect the working-memory guard.
  • All-family SIS/ISIS streams predictor columns; BED screening reduces packed two-bit genotypes directly with OpenMP. Retained-design fitting preserves original coefficient dimensions and criterion calibration. Training-only imputation is reused for prediction and relearned inside CV and bootstraps.
  • Ward outcome clustering streams row blocks, including its cut losses and aggregation. Explicit memory guards bound working matrices and outputs.
  • Native file-backed LASSO through optional biglasso reuses double bigmemory designs across training/CV row views. Gaussian, logistic, grouped Gaussian and Breslow Cox paths use the common likelihood scoring, IC selection and CV.

Simulation, comparison and interpretation

  • sparseGLM() compares supported sparse-regression methods with common likelihood, prediction, coefficient and support-recovery metrics and timings. Shared SIS/ISIS options screen every adapter, with method-specific ISIS offsets, original-dimension coefficients and training-only screening for CV.
  • Prediction, fitted-value, summary, likelihood and information-criterion methods, including within-row multichannel sparsity metrics.
  • Generic simulations, fixed-PSF deconvolution examples, visualization tools, reproducible benchmarks and a mathematical algorithm appendix.
